key_insight: Two complementary deep neural networks can invert the design process for SRF cavities and transmon qubits, mapping desired quantum-hardware performance directly to candidate geometries.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster exploration of bosonic quantum hardware designs by reducing reliance on expensive iterative electromagnetic and circuit simulations.
method: DNN #1 generates SRF cavity geometries from target cavity observables.
DNN #2 generates transmon designs from target qubit-cavity metrics: coupling rate g, qubit frequency νq, and anharmonicity α.
Recovered candidates are re-simulated end-to-end to verify the inverse-design output.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that candidate designs match targets to within about 5% for cavities and 2% for transmons, validated by end-to-end re-simulation.
watch_item: Because the inverse problem is one-to-many, returned geometries may be non-unique and still require fabrication-aware validation before deployment.
paper_title: Neural-Network Inverse Design of SRF Cavities and Transmons for Bosonic Quantum Computation
